name: rea
description: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries.
one_liner: Lets an AI assistant peek inside any app, website, or program (even without its source code) and explain exactly how a feature works, so you can rebuild it yourself.
buyer: A product manager or indie founder at a small software company who wants to copy a specific competitor feature without hiring a reverse-engineering specialist.
business_use_cases: A startup founder points it at a competitor's app to understand exactly how a popular feature (like an onboarding flow or pricing gate) is built, then rebuilds a version for their own product.
A freelance consultant uses it to quickly document how an old, undocumented internal tool actually works before quoting a client on a rebuild or migration project.
A security researcher at a small firm uses the native-binary analysis to triage whether a suspicious desktop app is doing anything it shouldn't, as part of a paid vendor-risk review.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a 'competitor teardown' service: pay a flat fee, get a report showing exactly how a named competitor feature works and a build plan to replicate it.
Run a paid vendor-software risk-review service for small businesses evaluating a new desktop app before rolling it out company-wide.

steal_this: Pick one well-known app feature people complain is missing from a competitor tool, reverse-engineer how the original does it this weekend, and ship a minimal clone as a paid add-on.
